Issued at 212 PM CST Tue Nov 10 2026

Through Tonight:

Expect calm and relatively cool conditions coming off the 
pleasant, unseasonably mild afternoon. High-level clouds
overspreading the region from the northwest will likely prevent
temperatures from getting a bit cooler than they otherwise have
given the setup. This in turn may preclude much in the way of
shallow ground fog development. Will defer to our evening shift
for another look at the fog potential, also considering that
near-term guidance has been much too aggressive with simulated
fog coverage in recent nights. If conditions end up more 
favorable than current thinking for fog, the best chance appears
to be for locales near/southeast of I-55 outside of Chicago, 
particularly in portions of northwest Indiana.

Wednesday through Tuesday:

On Wednesday, a compact, vigorous clipper-like shortwave, and 
associated surface low will track across the region. Top-down 
saturation of antecedent dry air mass will likely take some time
to erode before scattered showers can fully break through. 
Initial radar echoes into interior northern IL and portions of 
central IL Wednesday morning may end up being virga and 
sprinkles. The progged surface low path from southeast IA early 
Wednesday and then across central IL and IN during the afternoon
should tend to keep the most robust shower activity closer to 
the low path (ie. favoring areas near/south of I-80). Modestly 
steepened mid- level lapse rates with the arrival of colder air 
aloft could yield a few lightning strikes near/south of US 
Highway 24 in the afternoon.

The departing shortwave will phase in with an amplifying upper 
trough across the eastern CONUS Wednesday night into Thursday, 
which will allow a much cooler airmass to descend into the 
region through the end of the week. 850 mb temps will bottom out
in the -4 to -8 Celsius range Thursday PM through Friday night.
While embedded mid-level vort lobes rounding the resultant 
closed upper low may bring a few showers farther inland through 
the day on Thursday, focus continues to be on the persistent 
signal for a robust band of lake effect showers to set up over 
Lake Michigan, potentially into or through Saturday morning. 
This continues to seem reasonable at this distance given 
favorable lake-induced thermodynamics and prolonged northerly 
fetch. While occasional westward wobbles in the position of the 
band may occur, recent model cycles have continued to favor the
banding focusing mainly into northwest Indiana late Wednesday 
night onward.

The brisk full-fetch northerly flow is expected to propel a
marine modified (milder with higher wet bulb temps) air mass
fairly far inland during the coldest periods (nighttime and
early to mid morning) Thursday night into Saturday. In 
addition, the lowest forecast 850 mb temps over Lake Michigan 
are not nearly as cold as those of November 9-10, 2025, and
antecedent ground temps will also be notably warmer. The 
boundary layer thermal profile as such appears likely to be 
fairly marginal in the heart of the lake induced convergence 
band(s). Therefore, confidence is on the lower side regarding 
how far inland a primarily rain p-type will extend, and where 
p-type may mix with or even change to wet snow. Ultimately, 
while there has been some ensemble support for slushy 
accumulations into portions of interior northwest Indiana, an 
impactful wet lake effect snow does not appear to be the most 
likely scenario at this time. With all of this said, we will 
continue to monitor trends closely. Winds will also be strong 
near the lakeshore in Indiana and adjacent northeast Illinois, 
with gusts up to 35-40 mph at times during this period.

In addition to the much cooler daytime temperatures (40s)
Thursday through Saturday, inland areas away from the lake 
effect clouds will likely see temperatures fall solidly below 
freezing Thursday night through Saturday night. Long-range 
ensemble guidance indicates the colder pattern will be fairly 
short-lived as upper ridging builds back into the region early 
to mid next workweek, bringing a return to above normal temps 
for mid-November.

Castro/Petr
